label: Queso blanco
note: The Latin American fresh cheese, made by curdling hot milk with acid (or sometimes rennet) and pressed lightly, so softer than paneer, a different cheese

about.text: Queso blanco is a fresh white cheese of Latin America and the Caribbean, made by curdling hot milk with acid (or sometimes rennet) and lightly pressing the curd. It is soft, mild and does not melt.

how.text: Queso blanco is made like paneer or chhena: heating the milk to at least 85 °C and adding food acid makes the protein clot without rennet or starter. The curd is drained, salted and lightly pressed in hoops, so it is firm but moist and, because it is acid-set, does not melt when heated.

steps.name: acidify
steps.note: With an organic acid to pH about 5.3; the acid, not rennet, precipitates the protein.

steps.name: press
steps.note: In hoops, to remove excess whey.
